decisions.title: Replace hourly GitHub Pages PNG commits with a stateless Vercel HTML endpoint
decisions.summary: Retired the hourly hermes -> Grok PNG -> git push -> GitHub Pages pipeline in favor of a stateless Vercel web handler (api/index.ts) screenshotted directly by TRMNL's Screenshot plugin with Vercel Edge stale-while-revalidate caching and zero database.
decisions.resolution: Committing three PNGs per hour bloated .git past 2.4 GB and produced repetitive visuals, whereas Vercel aligns with existing team deployment habits and serves cached HTML well inside TRMNL's 5-second screenshot timeout.

comments.body: Running an hourly job on hermes that commits generated images to Git and serves them via GitHub Pages is blowing up the repo and visually boring; I normally push to Vercel and want a simple black-and-white HTML page TRMNL can screenshot directly with LLM logic inside the function.

Pure client-side browser fetch hits upstream CORS walls and risks snapping blank boxes under TRMNL's 5-second timeout, so a stateless Vercel serverless handler backed by CDN s-maxage=900 and stale-while-revalidate=86400 keeps everything server-rendered without a database.

decisions.title: Rotate five single-focus counter-readable posters every 15 minutes instead of a dense multi-widget page or raw LLM CSS
decisions.summary: Built five deterministic 800x480 1-bit HTML/CSS/SVG poster archetypes (dispatch, broadsheet, handbill, almanac, poster) with a 14px-76px type floor, >=2.5px SVG strokes, 15-minute rotation, and a strict village-storefront editorial boundary.
decisions.resolution: A counter-mounted 7.5-inch (~130 DPI) 1-bit TRMNL panel turns dense multi-column newspaper layouts into unreadable micro-print, while unconstrained LLM CSS risks clipping or dead space in front of shop customers.

comments.body: We display this at the store counter, so it needs visual variety inside structured templates and a community storefront boundary rather than household reminders or national partisan fights.
The initial multi-column broadsheet has way too much tiny detail for TRMNL e-ink; apply TRMNL display legibility guidance so each screen reads cleanly across a counter.

Redesigned all five archetypes into single-focus posters (~35-50 words per card, 14px minimum labels, 76px hero figures, >=2.5px strokes) that rotate every 15 minutes so customers get counter-distance legibility without losing breadth.

decisions.title: Enforce hard calendar gates in TypeScript before seasonal spotlight routing
decisions.summary: Restricted seasonal topics to hard date-bounded windows in TypeScript before invoking the Parallel Decisions API, and confined the winner to a bounded Seasonal Spotlight slot rather than overriding the entire edition.
decisions.resolution: Unbounded float-score competition previously allowed November freeze-thaw swings to trigger maple-sap headlines and crowd out town news.

comments.body: The old seasonal logic kept misfiring—claiming sap was running in November—and crowded out actual local updates, so gate seasonal topics strictly by calendar window.

decisions.title: Standardize 100% on Parallel Web Systems for extraction, decisions, and synthesis (and forbid pre-Gemini-4 models)
decisions.summary: Removed @google/genai and GEMINI_API_KEY completely, routing live web and PDF extraction (/v1/extract, /v1/search), editorial triage (/v1/decisions), and structured JSON copy/Chronicle synthesis (/v1beta/chat/completions) exclusively through Parallel Web Systems with secrets managed in the Cornwall Dispatch 1Password vault via fnox.
decisions.resolution: Consolidating onto Parallel eliminates multi-vendor API key sprawl while meeting all structured JSON, search, extraction, and rubric-decision needs under a single PARALLEL_API_KEY (with an explicit repo policy never to use any Gemini model prior to Gemini 4 if Gemini is ever introduced).

comments.body: Never use anything before Gemini 4, and why carry a separate Gemini dependency at all if Parallel can handle all of our extraction, decision, and LLM synthesis needs?
Verified Parallel /v1beta/chat/completions supports strict json_schema outputs alongside /v1/decisions, /v1/search, and /v1/extract.
Let's go 100% Parallel and store PARALLEL_API_KEY and CRON_SECRET in the dedicated Cornwall Dispatch vault in thefocusai.1password.com.

decisions.title: Feature notable upcoming Cornwall Chronicle calendar events on the Almanac poster instead of wildlife trivia
decisions.summary: Replaced the Almanac poster's bottom-right Nature Notes trivia box with an ON THE CALENDAR spotlight (with date pill) showcasing marquee upcoming Cornwall Chronicle gatherings while filtering out routine municipal board and Zoom meetings.
decisions.resolution: Generic wildlife snippets extracted from essays (such as 'Flying Squirrel') were unremarkable on a shop counter compared to upcoming community gatherings.

comments.body: Showing 'Flying Squirrel' on the Almanac screen isn't notable to anyone; replace that slot with something genuinely notable from the town calendar.

decisions.title: Prime /api/chronicle then / over HTTP inside GET /api/cron instead of synthesizing in-process
decisions.summary: Changed remote GET /api/cron executions to warm GET /api/chronicle first (24h Edge CDN cache) and then GET / (15m Edge CDN cache), reading X-Dispatch-* summary headers from the root response rather than calling buildStorefrontEdition() directly in api/cron.ts.
decisions.resolution: In-process synthesis inside api/cron.ts bypassed the /api/chronicle Edge cache and triggered a second full synthesis pass when touching /, pushing cold invocations past Vercel's 60-second FUNCTION_INVOCATION_TIMEOUT (504); sequential Edge priming cut cold cron execution to ~20.6s with zero duplicate LLM calls.

comments.body: First live production smoke test of /api/cron timed out at 60,053ms (504) because Isolate A synthesized in-process with forceRefresh while Isolate B repeated the full cold Chronicle PDF + Parallel pass for /; priming /api/chronicle then / over HTTP resolved the timeout and halved Parallel API usage.

decisions.title: Delete dead legacy files now and defer hermes cron retirement and Git history rewrite until physical TRMNL cutover
decisions.summary: Deleted unused shell scripts (setup.sh, run.sh), Python tests, legacy research reports, package-lock.json, and .github/workflows/pages.yml from main immediately, leaving hermes cron shutdown and any optional Git history compaction until after the physical TRMNL Screenshot plugin is pointed at Vercel.
decisions.resolution: Removing dead code keeps the repository clean without risking a blank screen on the store TRMNL before its dashboard URL is switched over.

comments.body: Clean up all the unused legacy junk right now—if we don't use it we don't need it—and cut over the TRMNL device once Vercel is live.

decisions.title: Expose /admin publicly without secrets and persist run history in cloud KV/Blob with a zero-daemon local JSON fallback
decisions.summary: Added an unlisted public Pressroom Admin route (/admin and /api/admin) exposing zero secret values, backed by Upstash Redis REST (UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL + UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN) or Vercel Blob (BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN) in production and an automatic gitignored local JSON fallback (logs/dispatch-history.json) when cloud credentials are unset.
decisions.resolution: Cloud KV/Blob survives serverless cold starts on Vercel, while automatic file fallback gives mise run dev durable local history with zero background redis-server daemon to manage.

comments.body: Asked whether /admin should be public like /?frame=1 or gated by CRON_SECRET, and whether run history should stay ephemeral in-memory or use a persistent cloud store.

I want /admin open as an unlisted public route like /?frame=1 and /api/state (with zero secrets exposed), and run history stored in a persistent cloud backend (Upstash Redis / Vercel KV or Vercel Blob).
Should we also run a local Redis instance for local development, or use something simpler?
Kept automatic fallback to gitignored logs/dispatch-history.json whenever cloud env vars are absent so local development persists across restarts without installing or running a local Redis daemon.

decisions.title: Extract Cornwall Chronicle PDFs via Parallel POST /v1/extract (dynamic fetch policy) before two-track structured synthesis, keeping page-aware unpdf only as an origin-WAF fallback
decisions.summary: Switched Cornwall Chronicle PDF ingestion to call Parallel POST /v1/extract first (omitting overriding fetch_policy limits so Parallel uses its indexed PDF cache and native 15s-60s PDF fetch window like platform.parallel.ai/play/extract), retained page-by-page unpdf + display-font de-kerning strictly as an origin-WAF HTTP 202 fallback, and routed content into concurrent Calendar/Flyer vs Editorial/Lore json_schema passes.
decisions.resolution: POST /v1/extract natively converts multi-page PDFs into clean Markdown without blind character slicing, while two focused /v1beta/chat/completions schemas turn that Markdown into typed YYYY-MM-DD events and briefs without exceeding output token timeouts.

comments.body: Check whether Parallel has a native extractor (platform.parallel.ai/play/extract), switch over to the real extractor rather than relying solely on local PDF parsing, and route the Chronicle extraction more intelligently.

Switched to POST /v1/extract with default dynamic fetch_policy (removing an artificial 24h max_age_seconds + 12s timeout that had tripped cornwallchronicle.org's WAF), split full-issue Markdown cleanly across paragraph boundaries so pages 4-7 are never truncated, and ran Calendar/Flyer and Editorial/Lore schemas concurrently.

decisions.title: Enforce visible prior-year attribution on Broadsheet headline + deck and rank current briefs ahead of retrospectives
decisions.summary: Added eventDate and isRetrospective metadata to Chronicle briefs so expired hearing notices are dropped and current-month developments rank ahead of prior-year lookbacks, updated /admin to badge Poster-only body copy, and added ensureVisibleYearAttribution() so any past year (< currentYear) cited in leadStory.body is deterministically surfaced in leadStory.headline and leadStory.deck.
decisions.resolution: The Broadsheet poster omits leadStory.body by design, so tucking '2024 election' inside body while running 'Cornwall Tops State in Voter Turnout' in headline/deck misled readers into thinking a 2024 Democracy Cup essay was 2026 election news.

comments.body: The extracted data for 'Cornwall Tops State in Voter Turnout' (90.46% Democracy Cup) notes in the body that it was the 2024 election, but the storefront display omits 2024 so it looks like a 2026 result.

Traced the bug to Page 2 of November_2026.pdf (a 2024 turnout lookback) combined with renderTownBulletinPoster hiding leadStory.body on Broadsheet; added temporal brief filtering/ranking, explicit Broadsheet visibility rules in the synthesis prompt, and a deterministic TypeScript year-attribution guard on headline + deck.

decisions.title: Provision Upstash Redis or Vercel Blob in Vercel Storage during /admin production rollout
decisions.summary: Implemented full Upstash Redis REST and Vercel Blob persistence in src/history.ts and declared optional env keys in fnox.toml, deferring live cloud store provisioning in Vercel Storage until owner-approved production deployment of /admin.
decisions.resolution: Deploying to production and modifying Vercel project infrastructure require explicit owner release approval per AGENTS.md, and /admin degrades cleanly to /tmp with an explicit notice banner until KV or Blob credentials are attached.
